The test image shows a tomato stem with:
- White/bleached rotted tissue at a node/stem section
- Small dark black specks scattered across the white area (possible sclerotia or pycnidia)
- Dead/dried stem tissue visible on the right
- White cottony material on the lesion

This points to a stem disease. Top candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Blight**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**. Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Stem close-up with white/bleached rotted tissue at a node
- Small black dots scattered on the white area (consistent with sclerotia forming)
- Dead/desiccated stem tissue on the right
- White cottony/powdery material on the lesion

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (Bugwood_12): Shows whole-plant wilting from stem rot — consistent disease pattern (white stem rot + sclerotia)
- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): White fluffy mycelium at soil line — similar white mycelium but sclerotia would be tan/brown, not black; typically more cord-like mycelial strands
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** (Bugwood_4): Dark brown/black canker at soil line — doesn't match the white bleached appearance
- **Gray_Mold** (Bugwood_13): Botrytis on fruit — no match

**Conclusion:** The white bleached stem tissue with scattered small black structures (developing sclerotia) is most characteristic of **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*). The black internal/surface sclerotia on bleached, girdled stem tissue is a hallmark of this disease. Southern Blight was the main alternative but its sclerotia are tan/brown and mustard-seed-shaped, not small black dots.
